_comment: Hierarchical risk taxonomy v3, from the final report Appendix A (Tables A1, A2, A4 and A5). Three families (A-C) hold nine domains, which keep the workbook codes R1-R9. Child risks are the unit of assessment: a control cites a child ID such as B.2.1, never a family or domain alone. Domain ids and child ids are POSITIONAL - the second domain of B is always B.2 - so if you insert one, renumber the rest. "owasp" maps the domain to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications; C.2 has no clean counterpart and says so.

domains.name: Objective & instruction integrity
domains.scenario: The agent replies to customers with inappropriate or conflicting policy information.
domains.triggers: Ambiguous instructions. Prompt injection. Malicious external content.
domains.controlThemes: Goal validation, intent confirmation, prompt-injection controls, stop conditions.

domains.name: Autonomy, authority & permission
domains.scenario: The agent approves unverified high-value transactions beyond its intended authority limit.
domains.triggers: Misconfigured permissions. Excessive credentials. Delegated authority.
domains.controlThemes: Least privilege, role-based access, action allowlists, approval gates.

domains.name: Tool & action execution
domains.scenario: The agent executes a DELETE command instead of READ on a production database.
domains.triggers: Model error. Tool ambiguity. Poor validation. API changes.
domains.controlThemes: Tool allowlisting, input validation, sandboxing, rollback, limits.

domains.name: Data, memory & information boundaries
domains.scenario: The agent emails a consolidated report containing external personal data.
domains.triggers: Malicious input. Weak access control. Untrusted memory.
domains.controlThemes: Data minimisation, loss prevention, encryption, retention limits, memory governance.

domains.name: Planning, workflow & delegation
domains.scenario: The agent gets stuck in an infinite loop, consuming API credits and blocking processes.
domains.triggers: Planning error. Missing dependencies. Conflicting outputs.
domains.controlThemes: Step validation, bounded workflows, execution limits, checkpoints.

domains.name: Agent-to-agent & ecosystem interaction
domains.scenario: A compromised third-party API allows an attacker to control internal agents.
domains.triggers: Compromised third party. Weak agent identity. Unverified messages.
domains.controlThemes: Identity verification, secure messaging, isolation, inter-agent logging.

domains.name: Human control, accountability & trust
domains.scenario: Human operators rubber-stamp a batch of flawed refunds.
domains.triggers: Poor human-in-the-loop design. Alert fatigue. Ambiguous accountability.
domains.controlThemes: Human-in-the-loop, dual approval, human override, clear ownership.

domains.name: Observability, traceability & auditability
domains.scenario: Auditors cannot determine why the agent granted a specific loan application.
domains.triggers: Logging gaps. Poor telemetry. Distributed systems.
domains.controlThemes: Immutable logs, trace IDs, monitoring, audit trails, provenance capture.

domains.name: Behavioural stability & runtime drift
domains.scenario: After a silent model update, the agent begins prioritising speed over accuracy.
domains.triggers: Model update. Environmental change. Memory accumulation.
domains.controlThemes: Runtime monitoring, behavioural baselines, kill switch, revalidation.

amplificationFactors.name: Irreversible actions
amplificationFactors.description: Actions that cannot be undone, such as deleting data or transferring funds.

amplificationFactors.name: External impacts
amplificationFactors.description: Actions directly affecting customers, external systems or the public.

amplificationFactors.name: Sensitive data
amplificationFactors.description: Access to personal data, health records, financial data or intellectual property.

amplificationFactors.name: Financial impact
amplificationFactors.description: High transaction limits, or access to corporate payment systems.

amplificationFactors.name: Vulnerable users
amplificationFactors.description: Interaction with minors, elderly users, or users in crisis.

amplificationFactors.name: Execution velocity
amplificationFactors.description: The agent's ability to repeat an error thousands of times in seconds.
